processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Standard induction melting in an alumina crucible under inert gas.
Drop cast into a 25 mm diameter cylindrical copper mould to produce samples with grain size of the order of 0.25 mm.
Cooling after solidification was sufficiently slow to allow a high degree of B2 order for Al-rich alloys and a good degree of DO3 order for alloys containing 25–30% Al.
Compression samples were cut from the ingots by spark machining, either as 3 mm diameter or as 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section samples, of height twice the diameter or width.

processing_steps.method: polishing on fine (1500 grade) abrasive paper
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Flat surfaces were polished on fine (1500 grade) abrasive paper before testing.

Tested at room temperature to a strain of 2–3% at a nominal strain rate of 3×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; the compression axis was always parallel to the cylinder axis of the cast samples; compression tests showed a smooth onset of plasticity, with no discrete yield points and slightly curved stress–strain behaviour.

Thin samples were cut from the centre of the deformed samples perpendicular to the stress axis using a diamond saw; thin foils for TEM were prepared with a twin-jet electropolishing unit using a 25% nitric acid in methanol mixture at about 20 V and −30 °C.

structures.overall_structure: Disordered / short-range-ordered Fe–20% Al (+0.1% B) after 2–3% room-temperature compression: plasticity is carried by singly gliding (1/2)⟨111⟩ dislocations that are generally smoothly curved with some preference for screw orientations, showing a weak tendency to cluster into an incipient cell structure, and with many of the segments being dipoles together with occasional small dipole loops.

microstructure_list.region: thin foil from the centre of the deformed sample

phases_present.phase_name: Fe–Al solid solution (disordered bcc / short-range ordered)

defects.type: single dislocations of Burgers vector (1/2)⟨111⟩, generally smoothly curved with some preference for screw orientations
dislocation dipoles (single-dislocation dipoles), edge dipole segments and occasional small dipole loops

microstructure_list.region: thin foil (wedge-shaped), centre of the deformed sample

phases_present.phase_name: Fe–Al solid solution (disordered bcc / short-range ordered)

defects.type: straight (screw-orientation) single dislocations, sometimes loosely paired
narrow edge dipole segments and many small dipole loops produced by trailing from the gliding screw dislocations

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression: 3 mm diameter or 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section, height twice diameter/width
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Deformed in compression to 2–3% strain; work hardening rate measured as the secant to the curving flow stress–strain line over the 1–1.5% strain range (strain range variation 0.5–1% or 1–2% gives similar results).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: flow stress and work hardening rate

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2010 microscope; dislocations imaged in Bright Field and Weak Beam modes; planar (shear or thermal) faults observed in various dark field modes
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: thin foils electropolished in 25% nitric acid in methanol at ~20 V and −30 °C; imaging with various g vectors to identify Burgers vectors
characterization_methods.purpose: examine the dislocation structures produced by room-temperature deformation
characterization_methods.key_findings: In the disordered/short-range-ordered Fe–20% Al material plasticity proceeds by single (1/2)⟨111⟩ dislocations that are smoothly curved with some screw preference; many segments are dipoles and occasional small loops occur; straight near-screw dislocations with narrow edge dipole segments and small dipole loops are also seen.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; 2–3% strain; nominal strain rate 3×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹
characterization_methods.purpose: measure flow stress and work hardening behaviour
characterization_methods.key_findings: Smooth onset of plasticity, no discrete yield points, and always slightly curved stress–strain behaviour, with no linear stress–strain regions.

unmapped_findings: The dislocation-structure micrographs and descriptions for the low-Al-content material (Figs. 5–7 and b0031) are labelled 'Fe–20% Al' / 'materials containing 15 and 20% Al' and do not explicitly state the 0.1% B content; they have been assigned here to the 20% Al composition class that includes this sample, but they may correspond to the binary Fe–20% Al composition.

Fig. 1 gives the yield stress and ductility of polycrystalline Fe–Al alloys versus Al content but does not distinguish the B-containing alloy; at 20% Al the ductility is about 25% and the yield stress increases steadily up to 25% Al, but no specific value is reported for the 20% Al + 0.1% B sample.

The work hardening rate peak (maximum measured over the 1–1.5% strain range) occurs in the 26–29% Al range (near 29% Al) for the ordered Fe–Al alloys; the 20% Al material lies on the low disordered plateau of the work hardening curve (Fig. 2).
The cast ingot grain size for all alloys in the study is of the order of 0.25 mm (b0022).
